replies.body: We already have most of jmx metrics use `mean` so it's simpler to leave it as-is rather than changing it. We know that there is a small inconsistency in activemq, we can change that later if needed.

I asked copilot to research the semconv repo:

> review usage of "average" vs "mean" in metric names
>
> and any discussions that happened about those choices on the related PRs where they were added

and it gave me:

## PR Discussions

### [PR #991](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/pull/991) (Node.js metrics)

No discussion about "mean" vs "average" naming. The discussion focused on whether the namespace should be `nodejs` vs `js` vs `jsruntime`, and why `gauge` was used instead of `histogram`. The use of `.mean` was accepted without comment — it directly matches the Node.js API surface (`histogram.mean`).

### [PR #2283](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/pull/2283) (K8s HPA CPU metrics)

No discussion about "average" naming. The review focused on entity associations, attribute requirements, and conflicts. The use of `average_value` and `average_utilization` was accepted without comment — it directly mirrors the Kubernetes API field names.

-------

my opinion:

If we want to pick one, I'd suggest "average". I think it's more common, and the k8s naming tends to be pretty well thought out from what I've seen.

It's also reasonable to vary the choice based on the term used by the underlying jmx metric (similar to what node.js did).

The question here is only about the naming of the aggregated metric and choosing between
- consistency: suggest to always use "mean" or "average", then it could provide some uniformity for the consumers of the metric, for example if tomcat exposes an average response time and another application server does the same then it would be nice of both were following a common .mean or .average naming convention.
- stay close the the implementation: suggest to use either "mean" or "average" and picking what is closest to the underlying implementation (in the case of JMX, it would fit the MBean attribute name and/or description), the nice think about this is that it could be less challenging for consumers to understand the link to implementation.

While I tend to prefer consistency, I think it could be fine to preserve the naming of the underlying implementation. Choosing this option also have the benefit to work with existing choices we've made so far:
- for `activemq`: `message.enqueue.average_duration` metric from `AverageEnqueueTime` MBean attribute (*)
- for `camel`: `exchange.processing.duration.mean` metric from `MeanProcessingTime` MBean attribute

Unless there is strong arguments for not doing this, I will update this PR to reflect that when we must choose between "mean" or "average" then we choose what is closest to the underlying implementation (in case of JMX, the MBean attribute name). As summarized above and in the semconv slack discussion this is what has been picked for node in the past: https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C041APFBYQP/p1771601931619829

(*): we could still want to rename it to `message.enqueue.duration.average` though, but this is not the aspect we are discussing here.
@SylvainJuge sounds reasonable. I think this PR would be ready for merging after these changes are made.

I've settled to recommend using whatever is closer to the underlying implementation, the lack of "consistency" is unlikely to be an issue as those pre-aggregated metrics are also very unlikely to be shared across different products.
